extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, recipients, institutional grants administrators, and NIH grants management officials
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and policy standards from the NIH Grants Policy (glossary) describing required terms, responsibilities, and procedural requirements for applying for, managing, and reporting on NIH Federal awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity that receives a contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allocation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Central service or public assistance cost allocation plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost objective
rubrics_metrics.description: A program, function, activity, award, organizational subdivision, contract, or work unit for which cost data are desired and for which provision is made to accumulate and measure the cost of processes, products, jobs and capital projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cost objective may be a major function of the recipient or subrecipient, a particular service or project, a Federal award, or an indirect cost activity, as described in 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart E—Cost Principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost overrun
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amount charged in excess of the Federal share of costs for the project period (competitive segment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The government-wide principles established under 2 CFR Part 200 for determining the allowable costs incurred by non-Federal entities under Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principles are for the purpose of cost determination and are not intended to identify the circumstances or dictate the extent of Federal Government participation in financing. They ensure Federal awards bear their fair share of cost except where restricted by statute. Hospitals follow 2 CFR Part 200, Appendix IX; for-profit organizations follow FAR (48 CFR Part 31.2). See Cost Considerations—The Cost Principles for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: The portion of project costs not paid by Federal funds or contributions (unless authorized by Federal statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This term includes matching, which refers to required levels of cost share that must be provided. See 2 CFR Part 200.306.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing or matching alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternative use of program income whereby income accrued during the period of grant support may be used to satisfy a cost sharing or matching requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also additive alternative and deductive alternative and Administrative Requirements—Management Systems and Procedures—Program Income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-type contract
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract or subcontract under a grant in which the contractor or subcontractor is paid on the basis of the allowable costs it incurs, with or without a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and safety monitoring plan
rubrics_metrics.description: For each NIH-supported clinical trial, NIH requires a data and safety monitoring plan that will provide oversight and monitoring to ensure the safety of participants and the validity and integrity of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The level of monitoring should be commensurate with the risks and the size and complexity of the clinical trial. A detailed plan must be submitted to the applicant’s IRB and subsequently to the awarding IC for approval prior to the accrual of human subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of validating, organizing, protecting, maintaining, and processing scientific data to ensure the accessibility, reliability, and quality of the scientific data for its users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMS Plan) / Data Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: A plan describing the data management, preservation, and sharing of scientific data and accompanying metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data sharing is the act of making scientific data available for use by others (e.g., the larger research community, institutions, the broader public), for example, via an established repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment and suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The actions taken by a debarring official in accordance with OMB guidance at 2 CFR Part 180, as implemented by HHS in 2 CFR Part 376, to exclude a person or organization from participating in grants and other non-procurement awards government-wide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If debarred or suspended, the person or organization may not receive financial assistance (under a grant, cooperative agreement, or subaward, or contract under a grant) for a specified period of time. Debarments and suspensions under 2 CFR Part 376 are distinct from post-award suspension action by an awarding agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of collecting funds owed by recipients to the Federal government, which, under grants, generally are owed as a result of formal cost disallowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: A document used to record a legal obligation of one party to pay a financial obligation to another in accordance with predetermined terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deductive alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternative for the use of program income earned during the period of grant support under which allowable costs of the project or program to be paid by the Federal government are offset by the amount of the program income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also additive alternative and cost sharing or matching alternative and Administrative Requirements—Management Systems and Procedures—Program Income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental Grants Appeals Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent office established in the Office of the Secretary with delegated authority to review and decide certain disputes between recipients of HHS funds and HHS awarding agencies under 45 CFR Part 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performed review, adjudication and mediation services as assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviation
rubrics_metrics.description: A departure on a single-case or class basis from a regulatory or policy requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single-case deviation is a request for waiver or exception sought for one grant only; a class deviation involves more than one grant for which the same type of deviation action is being requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs that can be identified specifically with a particular sponsored project, an instructional activity, or any other institutional activity, or that can be directly assigned to such activities relatively easily with a high degree of accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges to a Federal award that the Federal agency or pass-through entity determines to be unallowable, in accordance with applicable Federal statutes, regulations, provisions of 2 CFR Part 200, or the terms and conditions of the Federal award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary Award
rubrics_metrics.description: An award in which NIH, exercising judgment, selects the recipient or the amount of funding through a competitive process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, NIH awards are discretionary. See Non-Discretionary Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A public (including a State or other governmental agency) or private non-profit or for-profit organization that is located in the United States or its territories, is subject to U.S. laws, and assumes legal and financial accountability for awarded funds and for the performance of the grant-supported activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Stage Investigator (ESI)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who is classified as a New Investigator and is within 10 years of completing their terminal research degree or is within 10 years of completing medical residency (or the equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See definition of New Investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity Identification Number
rubrics_metrics.description: A three-part coding scheme of 12 characters used in PMS to identify organizations and individuals. The first character identifies the recipient as an organization or an individual; the next nine characters are the Employer Identification Number; the last two characters are a suffix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also known as Payment System Identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tangible personal property (including information technology systems) having a useful life of more than one year and a per-unit acquisition cost that equals or exceeds the lesser of the capitalization level established by the recipient or subrecipient for financial statement purposes, or $10,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also capital assets, computing devices, general purpose equipment, information technology systems, special purpose equipment, and supplies.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: The Electronic Research Administration virtual meeting place where NIH extramural recipient organizations, recipients, and the public can receive and transmit information about the administration of biomedical and behavioral research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divided into unrestricted and restricted portions for public and confidential information, respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard term of all NIH awards to allow recipients several flexibilities to waive the requirement for prior approval for specified actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH extended expanded authorities to all NIH awards except for the provision to automatically carry over unobligated balances for certain awards. See Administrative Requirements—Changes in Project and Budget—NIH Standard Terms of Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditure report
rubrics_metrics.description: Means: (1) For non-construction grants, the SF-425 Federal Financial Report (FFR) (or other OMB-approved equivalent report); (2) for construction grants, the SF-271 'Outlay Report and Request for Reimbursement' (or other OMB-approved equivalent report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditures (reporting rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges made by a recipient or subrecipient to a project or program for which a Federal award is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be reported on cash or accrual basis if methodology is disclosed and consistently applied. For cash-basis reports, expenditures are sum of cash disbursements for direct charges; indirect expense charged; value of third-party in-kind contributions applied; and cash advance payments and payments to subrecipients. For accrual basis, expenditures are sum of cash disbursements for direct charges; indirect expense incurred; value of third-party in-kind contributions applied; and net increase or decrease in amounts owed for goods received, services performed, and programs for which no current services are required (e.g., annuities, insurance claims). See definition of 'indirect costs.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal agency (agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'agency' as defined at 5 U.S.C. 551(1) and 5 U.S.C. 552(f); generally refers to the agency that provides a Federal award directly to a recipient unless context indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also definitions of Federal award and recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Audit Clearinghouse (FAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The repository of record designated by OMB where non-Federal entities must transmit the reporting packages required by Subpart F—Audit Requirements of 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart F – Audit Requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing address provided; future updates at the FAC website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and Administrative (F&A) costs (indirect costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred for a common or joint purpose benefitting more than one cost objective, and not readily assignable to the cost objectives specifically benefitted, without effort disproportionate to the results achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May require multiple pools of indirect costs to facilitate equitable distribution; indirect cost pools must be distributed on a basis that produces an equitable result considering relative benefits derived. For IHEs, the term F&A cost is often used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal award (definition/instrument)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on context, (1) the Federal financial assistance that a recipient receives directly from a Federal agency or indirectly from a pass-through entity as described in 2 CFR Part 200.101; or (2) the cost-reimbursement contract under the FAR that a non-Federal entity receives directly or indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also refers to the instrument setting forth the terms and conditions (grant agreement, cooperative agreement, other assistance instruments, or cost-reimbursement contract). Federal award does not include other contracts used to buy goods or services or contracts to operate GOCOs. See also definitions of Federal financial assistance, grant agreement, and cooperative agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal award date
rubrics_metrics.description: The date when the authorized official of the Federal agency signed (physically or digitally) the Federal award or when an alternative consistent with 31 U.S.C. 1501 is reached with the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct from the budget start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Award Identification Number (FAIN)
rubrics_metrics.description: A unique number assigned to a financial assistance award to assist recipients in correctly reporting subawards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public can use the FAIN and Assistance listing number to find awards in databases; NIH derives the FAIN from core elements of the grant number (example: 1R01HL654321-01 → R01HL654321).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal awarding agency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency that provides a Federal award directly to another entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also Awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Demonstration Partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: A cooperative initiative among some Federal agencies, selected organizations receiving Federal funding for research, and certain professional associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts include demonstration projects intended to simplify and standardize Federal requirements to increase research productivity and reduce administrative costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance that non-Federal entities receive or administer in the form of: grants; cooperative agreements; non-cash contributions or donations of property; direct appropriations; food commodities; and other financial assistance (except certain exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 2 CFR Part 200.202 and Subpart F, also includes loans, loan guarantees, interest subsidies, and insurance. Does not include amounts received as reimbursement for services rendered to individuals described in 2 CFR Part 200.502(h) and (i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal institution
rubrics_metrics.description: A Cabinet-level department or independent agency of the executive branch or any component organization of such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in this document in context of a Federal institution as a recipient. See also Awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal interest
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of 2 CFR Part 200.330 or when used in connection with acquisition or improvement of real property, equipment, or supplies under a Federal award, the dollar amount that is the product of: (1) Federal share of total project costs; and (2) current fair market value of the property/improvements, to the extent acquisition/improvement costs were included as project costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal program
rubrics_metrics.description: All Federal awards assigned a single number in the Assistance listings; when no Assistance listing number is assigned, all Federal awards from the same agency made for the same purpose should be combined and considered one program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clusters of programs include Research and Development (R&D), Student Financial Aid (SFA), and 'Other clusters' as described in Cluster of Programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal share
rubrics_metrics.description: The portion of the total project costs that are paid by Federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalwide Assurance (FWA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only type of assurance of compliance accepted and approved by OHRP for institutions engaged in nonexempt research involving human subjects conducted or supported by HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under an FWA, an institution commits to HHS that it will comply with requirements in 45 CFR Part 46 and the terms of assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An amount, in addition to actual, allowable costs, paid to an organization providing goods or services consistent with normal commercial practice; also referred to as profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Grants to For-Profit Organizations—SBIR/STTR Programs—Allowable Costs and Fee—Profit or Fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial conflict of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: A financial conflict of interest exists when the recipient’s designated official(s) reasonably determines that an investigator’s significant financial interest could directly and significantly affect the design, conduct, or reporting of the PHS-funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 42 CFR Part 50, Subpart F, Responsibility of Applicants for Promoting Objectivity in Research for which PHS funding is sought and Public Policy Requirements and Objectives—Financial Conflict of Interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed Award Amount
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of grant or cooperative agreement pursuant to which NIH or a pass-through entity provides a specific amount of funding without regard to actual costs incurred under the Federal award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign component
rubrics_metrics.description: The performance of any significant scientific element or segment of a project outside of the United States, either by the recipient or by a researcher employed by a foreign organization, whether or not grant funds are expended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities that meet this definition include involvement of human subjects or animals at a foreign site; extensive foreign travel for data collection; any activity that may impact U.S. foreign policy; collaborations anticipated to result in co-authorship; use of facilities at a foreign site; or receipt of financial support or resources from a foreign entity. Foreign travel for consultation is not considered a foreign component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign organization
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity that is (1) a public or private organization located in a country other than the United States and subject to that country's laws; (2) a private nongovernmental organization in another country that solicits contributions; (3) a charitable organization in another country that is nonprofit and tax-exempt under its laws and is not a university/hospital/etc.; or (4) an organization located in a country not recognized as a Foreign Public Entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign public entity
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign government or foreign governmental entity; a public international organization entitled to privileges and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act; an entity owned or controlled by a foreign government; or any other entity consisting wholly or partly of foreign governments or governmental entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: For-profit organization
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization organized to earn a profit, including corporations, partnerships, LLCs, and sole proprietorships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered a small business if independently owned and operated, not dominant in the field proposed, and employs no more than 500 persons. See small business concern definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of days per week and/or months per year representing full-time effort at the applicant/recipient organization, as specified in organizational policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization’s policy must be applied consistently regardless of the source of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: General purpose equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment not limited to research, medical, scientific, or other technical activities (examples: office equipment, furnishings, telephone networks, IT equipment and systems, air conditioning, reproduction and printing equipment, motor vehicles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also 'Equipment' and 'Special Purpose Equipment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Generally Acceptable Accounting Principles (GAAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaning specified in accounting standards issued by the GASB and the FASB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generally Accepted Government Auditing Standards (GAGAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Also known as the Yellow Book, GAGAS are generally accepted government auditing standards issued by the Comptroller General of the United States, which apply to financial audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant number
rubrics_metrics.description: A unique identifier for a grant composed of the application type code, activity code, Organizational Code, 6-digit serial number, support year and/or suffix code for the support year of the grant, or other information such as a supplement, resubmission, or fellowship institutional allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Federalwide systems the FAIN is used. Sample Grant Number: 1 R01 AI 123456-01 A1 S1. Sample FAIN: R01 AI 654321.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant or cooperative agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal instrument of financial assistance between a Federal agency and a recipient or between a pass-through entity and a subrecipient used to transfer anything of value to carry out a public purpose authorized by U.S. law and not to acquire property or services for the Federal agency's direct benefit or use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grant is distinguished from a cooperative agreement in that it does not provide for substantial involvement between the Federal agency or pass-through entity and the recipient. Does not include agreements that provide only direct cash assistance to individuals, subsidies, loans, loan guarantees, or insurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants Management Officer (GMO)
rubrics_metrics.description: An NIH official responsible for the business management aspects of grants and cooperative agreements, including review, negotiation, award, and administration, and for interpretation of grants administration policies and provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GMOs are delegated authority from the CGMO to obligate NIH to the expenditure of funds and permit changes to approved projects on behalf of NIH. Each NIH IC that awards grants has one or more GMOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants Management Specialist
rubrics_metrics.description: An NIH staff member who oversees the business and other non-programmatic aspects of one or more grants and/or cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include evaluating grant applications for administrative content and compliance, negotiating grants, providing consultation and technical assistance to recipients, and administering grants after award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: The single access point for all grant programs offered by 26 Federal grant-making agencies as designated by OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a single interface for agencies to announce opportunities and for applicants to find and apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant-supported project or activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Those activities specified or described in a grant application or subsequent submission that are approved by an NIH IC for funding, regardless of whether Federal funding constitutes all or only a portion of the financial support necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honoraria
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments given in support of professional services for purpose of conferring distinction or to symbolize respect, esteem, or admiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the service is related to research oversight, supervision, or co-authoring research papers, payments are not honoraria but considered research funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility licensed as a hospital under state law or operated as a hospital by the U.S., state, or subdivision; includes nonprofit or for-profit hospitals or a medical care provider component of a nonprofit organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human biospecimens
rubrics_metrics.description: A quantity of tissue, blood, urine, or other human-derived material; includes subcellular structures, cells, tissue, organs, blood, gametes, embryos, fetal tissue, waste, and biospecimens isolated and propagated into new cell lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single biopsy may generate several human biospecimens (e.g., multiple paraffin blocks or frozen samples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Fetal Tissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Tissue or cells obtained from a dead human embryo or fetus after spontaneous or induced abortion or stillbirth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include established human fetal cell lines. Research involving transplantation of human fetal tissue must comply with applicable Federal, State and local laws and NIH guidance. See also Human Fetal Tissue Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subject (Common Rule definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A living individual about whom an investigator obtains information or biospecimens through intervention or interaction and uses, studies, or analyzes them; or obtains, uses, studies, analyzes, or generates identifiable private information or identifiable biospecimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations extend to use of human organs, tissues, and body fluids from identifiable individuals and to graphic, written, or recorded information derived from such individuals. See Public Policy Requirements and Objectives—Human Subjects Protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: The rating assigned to an individual application by an SRG that designates the reviewers’ assessment of scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For research projects, defined as the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of established review criteria. Impact scores may be numeric (10–90) or alphabetical (ND). The SRG uses the impact score to make funding recommendations to the IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any payment that should not have been made or that was made in an incorrect amount (including overpayments and underpayments) under statutory, contractual, administrative, or other legally applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes payments to ineligible recipients; payments for ineligible goods/services; duplicate payments; payments for goods/services not received (except where authorized by law); payments not authorized by law; and payments not accounting for applicable discounts. See OMB Circular A-123 Appendix C for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Tribe (federally recognized Indian Tribe)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Indian Tribe, band, nation, or other organized group or community, including Alaska Native villages or regional/village corporations recognized as eligible for special U.S. programs because of their status as Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes tribes identified in the Bureau of Indian Affairs list and entities qualifying as Alaska Native villages or regional village corporations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information technology systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Computing devices, ancillary equipment, software, firmware, and similar procedures, services (including support services), and related resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also computing devices and equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Something new or improved, including research for development of new technologies, refinement of existing technologies, or development of new applications for existing technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PHS programs, examples include new medical or biological products for improved value, efficiency, or costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute or Center (IC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH organizational component responsible for a particular grant program or set of activities; the terms 'NIH IC' or 'awarding IC' designate a point of contact for advice and interpretation of grant requirements and for requesting prior approvals or changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IACUC appointed by the CEO or designee is federally mandated to oversee the institution's animal program, facilities, and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IACUC review and approval is required for all PHS supported activities involving live vertebrate animals prior to funding. Recipients must maintain an animal care and use program based on the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional base salary
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual compensation paid by an organization for an employee’s appointment, regardless of whether time is spent on research, teaching, patient care, or other activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base salary excludes income earned outside duties for the organization. Base salary may not be increased as a result of replacing organizational salary funds with NIH grant funds. See Cost Considerations—Allowability of Costs—Selected Items of Cost—Salaries and Wages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Review Board (IRB)
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative body established to protect the rights and welfare of human research subjects recruited to participate in research activities conducted under the auspices of the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IRB has authority to approve, require modifications in, or disapprove all research activities within its jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution of Higher Education (IHE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined at 20 U.S.C. 1001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intangible property
rubrics_metrics.description: Property having no physical existence, such as trademarks, copyrights, data (including data licenses), websites, IP licenses, trade secrets, patents, patent applications, loans, notes, lease agreements, stocks and other instruments of property ownership, software, or software subscriptions or licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intergovernmental Personnel Act (IPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mobility program that provides for temporary assignment of personnel between the Federal Government and state/local governments, colleges and universities, Indian Tribe governments, FFRDCs, and other eligible organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal is to facilitate movement of employees for short periods when movement serves a sound public purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control over compliance requirements for Federal awards
rubrics_metrics.description: A process implemented by recipients and subrecipients designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding achievement of objectives related to Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives include: (1) transactions properly recorded to permit reliable financial statements and reports, maintain accountability, and demonstrate compliance; (2) transactions executed in compliance with Federal statutes, regulations, and terms/conditions of the Federal award that could have a direct and material effect; and (3) funds, property, and other assets safeguarded against loss from unauthorized use or disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal controls
rubrics_metrics.description: A process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding achievement of objectives in: effectiveness and efficiency of operations; reliability of reporting for internal and external use; and compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: International organization
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization that identifies itself as international or intergovernmental and has membership from, and represents the interests of, more than one country, regardless of headquarters location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement pursuant to 37 CFR Part 401 that recipients of contracts, grants or cooperative agreements fully disclose any subject inventions made during the performance of work under a funding agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to protect the Federal government's rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigational new drug
rubrics_metrics.description: A new drug or biological drug that is used in a clinical investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator-initiated research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research funded as a result of an investigator, on their own, submitting a research application in response to Parent Announcements only (also known as unsolicited research).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPF number
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional Profile File number is a unique number used by NIH for tracking/reporting awards to recipient institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policy allowing submission of certain elements of a competing application to be deferred until later in the application process, after review when the application is under consideration for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within the Status module of the eRA Commons, users can submit Just-In-Time information when requested by NIH. Institutions can electronically submit information requested after review but before award. See Completing the Pre-Award Process—Just-In-Time Procedures.
